Question Choices: Enter the lower and upper bounds of the principal range of arcsin(x). Angles are in radians.
Hints: Sine is restricted to a one-to-one interval.|Use Quadrants IV and I with endpoints.
Solution: The principal arcsine returns the unique angle in [-pi/2,pi/2] whose sine equals the input. Its input domain is [-1,1], and both range endpoints are included. The principal range is [-pi/2, pi/2].

Solution: The principal arccosine returns the unique angle in [0,pi] whose cosine equals the input. Its input domain is [-1,1], and both range endpoints are included. The principal range is [0, pi].

Question Choices: Find arctan(1). Angles are in radians.
Hints: Choose the principal angle whose tangent is 1.|Sine and cosine are equal there.
Solution: The principal arctangent returns the unique angle in (-pi/2,pi/2) whose tangent equals the input. Every real input is allowed; the range endpoints are excluded. arctan(1) = pi/4.
